candidate.name: intraday_range_clock_center_240m
candidate.mechanism: First chronological moment of scale-free intrabar high-low range mass across the complete standard one-minute session
candidate.formula: For r_i=log(high_i/low_i) and x_i=i/239 over i=0,...,239, compute score=sum(x_i*r_i)/sum(r_i).
candidate.zero_rule: Exact zero-range bars remain zero masses. Require finite positive ordered high/low values on all 240 bars and finite strictly positive total range mass; use no epsilon, dropped bar, pseudocount, threshold, or substituted observation.
candidate.fixed_grid: Require the raw 09:30 row for source identity, use exactly 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00 in a fixed 240-position chronological grid, and exclude 09:30. No return, gap, or lunch price change is formed.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_volatility_resolution_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: both locate price uncertainty in session time
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor compares only total squared close-return mass in the morning versus afternoon and reads no high/low. Campaign090 uses all 240 high-low range masses on a continuous fixed clock, reads no close, and remains sensitive to within-half timing after half totals are fixed.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_intrabar_range_participation_entropy_240m and intraday_morning_afternoon_range_profile_similarity_120b
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Entropy is invariant to every clock permutation and profile similarity compares ordinal morning/afternoon shapes. Campaign090 is a signed chronological first moment and has no entropy or distribution-distance operator.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_range_amount_peak_timing_alignment_240m and intraday_range_amount_profile_alignment_js_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all use the range profile on the standard grid
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factors require amount and measure either one peak-time distance or two-distribution alignment. Campaign090 is amount invariant and uses the full marginal range profile's first clock moment.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_amount_center_of_mass_240m and intraday_amount_clock_dispersion_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all apply fixed clock moments to a nonnegative intraday mass profile
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those factors measure when transaction activity occurs or how dispersed it is. Campaign090 measures when scale-free price uncertainty is expressed, changes under high-low envelope interventions that leave amount fixed, and is invariant to arbitrary amount-path changes.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: late_return_30m, late_amount_share_30m, and intraday_terminal_bar_amount_share_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all may respond to late-session activity or price discovery
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factors use a fixed late cutoff or one terminal amount bar. Campaign090 uses no cutoff, return, or amount and assigns every range bar its preregistered continuous clock coordinate.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_extreme_arrival_order_240m, intraday_global_price_range_revisit_240m, intraday_two_sided_range_frontier_balance_238m, and intraday_close_frontier_innovation_share_238p
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: all react to price-range or frontier timing
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those mechanisms use global extrema, revisits, frontier expansions, or close innovations. Campaign090 ignores extrema identity and frontier state, using only the complete vector of same-bar high-low masses.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_range_share_volume_confirmation_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal confirmation factor relates range to share volume and discards clock center. Campaign090 reads no volume and changes under pure clock relocation with range/volume pairing otherwise irrelevant.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_directional_amount_timing_spread_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Campaign089 conditions destination amount on positive versus negative close-return signs and takes a difference of two conditional centers. Campaign090 reads neither amount nor close, has no direction labels, and takes one marginal high-low range center.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: candidate49_intraday_cumulative_vwap_crossing_rate_240m_v1
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: both use a completed intraday grid
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Candidate49 counts causal close-versus-cumulative-VWAP sign crossings and uses close/volume/amount. Campaign090 uses only high/low range masses, does not construct a price reference, and does not touch the prospective ledger.
